name: Deep Space Energy,
description: Deep Space Energy (DSE) is developing a new European radioisotope power system (RPS) built around its proprietary Radioisotope Dynamic Generator (RDG). The RDG achieves up to 5× higher fuel-to-power efficiency (per Watt-electric) compared to legacy RTGs, while also offering enhanced reliability. While the RDG is designed to be compatible with multiple radioisotope heat sources (RHS) and fuel forms, DSE is also advancing its own composite Sr-90 fuel and heat source, enabling delivery of the full power subsystem as an integrated solution. Target applications include: – Sub-kilowatt lunar surface power for surviving the lunar night and operating in permanently shadowed regions. – Auxiliary power for strategic space assets, providing resilience against non-kinetic threats.

description: DeltaVision GmbH is a deep & space tech start-up with focus on fluid management within propulsive and complementary systems for transport and mobility applications. Our unique expertise is the domain of valves for cryogenic and highly pressurized fluids, among others hydrogen, methane, oxygen and more. This knowledge we gained from a decade of contribution to the development of space transportation vehicles within major European space projects. We happily observe that cryogenic and highly pressurized fluidic systems evolve from niche applications in space towards mainly hydrogen driven mainstream applications on earth. One outstanding example here are the developments on hydrogen-based aeronautic. We’d love to take this opportunity and provide our knowledge, innovations & passion for fluidic management systems also to this uprising community. The mission of deltaVision is to become the customer’s choice and European reference for advanced and cryogenic Fluid Control Equipment in space transportation and hydrogen mobility applications.

description: detonext has set itself the goal of revolutionising combustion in heating systems and power generation. We want to further develop the technology of the rotating detonation engine to create a more powerful and efficient heating system that can meet the high energy demands of the non-residential building sector. Rotating detonation engines (RDEs) is a rocket engine concept that uses supersonic combustion to increase combustion efficiency by utilizing pressure gain combustion. We therefore intend to use this combustion process to develop an innovative, sustainable heating and power system which is able to deliver the same amount of energy for less fuel.

With an aging population and families more distant than ever, we are sleep walking into a care crisis. This new challenge needs a new solution – Robody Cares – that combines the benefits of modern technology with human care, ensuring that your loved ones are always well taken care of and receive the help they need. Combining AI, AR, and 5G, Robodies are human robotic avatars allowing its operator to teleport their senses, action, and presence anywhere on the planet or in space. This makes Robodies an alternative for space based operations in the future.

name: Dromos
description: ESA and its partners have established and proven technologies, such as satellite-based communication, which can be used to secure/replace the V2X channels in critical situations. The use of satellite-based services requires, among other things, the seamless handover of services between different technologies (from satellite to mobile and back), multiple redundancy strategies between complementary technologies to improve security and reliability, and localization via satellite vs. mobile network (triangulation vs. odometry). The ESA-BIC project aims to evaluate these alternative channels for dromos, verify their validity, reliability and cost-effectiveness, and prepare all this for a pilot application.

name: DronEye.
description: DronEye develops an additional device to make any drone an AI-powered drone for situational awareness during emergencies. The solution has two main components: First, the AI sensor (smart video streaming device start transmission when detecting victim or target) that can be mounted on drones to detect relevant objects such as victims and allows adaptive video & information streaming to a remote server. Second, the fleet management platform that response teams can use to remotely command drones and preview the received video stream from disaster zones. The drones can be flied pre-programmed routes passing through waypoints, which are defined, by GNSS co-ordinates and altitude levels. The drones have a GNSS receiver, which utilises the GNSS constellations to determine its position. Furthermore, the drones will be connected to the pilot through a communications link, which is comprised of 4G/LTE (i.e., mobile phone networks) and a SatCom links. While the signal strength of 4G can differ based on the drone’s location and altitude, SatCom is always present and ensures that the drone pilots are always able to monitor the performance of the drone and take control if required. The SatCom link is therefore a critical safety redundancy component of the overarching drone control system, whereas the additional SatEO allows remote monitoring of people, objects, and surrounding environments. 1DronEye develops an additional device to make any drone an AI-powered drone for situational awareness during emergencies.
